hints: Focus on what a strong absorption around 1720 cm-1 means, and check the table for which C=O containing groups fit there.
Notice Q has a C=O peak near 1700 cm-1 plus a strong, broad peak centred at 2800 cm-1, which matches the carboxyl O-H range of 2500-3000 cm-1.
Consider which type of carbonyl compound can be oxidised further by hot acidified dichromate(VI) to give a carboxylic acid.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional group in P**

P has 3 carbons and a strong peak at 1720 cm-1. From the table this is in the C=O region.

It fits carbonyl, carboxyl at 1670-1740 cm-1 and ester at 1710-1750 cm-1, so P contains a C=O bond, not just an alcohol O-H.

**Identify the functional group in Q**

Q shows C=O at 1700 cm-1 and a strong, broad absorption centred at 2800 cm-1.

That broad peak fits O-H in a carboxyl group at 2500-3000 cm-1, very different from a sharp hydroxy O-H at 3200-3600 cm-1. So Q is a carboxylic acid:
$$\text{R-COOH}$$

**Use oxidation to link Q back to P**

Hot excess acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is a strong oxidising agent. An aldehyde is oxidised to a carboxylic acid:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$
A ketone resists this oxidation, and an alcohol starting material would not show C=O at 1720 cm-1 in P.

**Conclude what P must be**

P must already contain C=O but still be oxidisable to an acid. That is exactly an aldehyde with three carbons, propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, oxidised to propanoic acid.

options.A: Propanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is a 3-carbon aldehyde. Its aldehyde C=O explains the 1720 cm-1 peak in P, and oxidation with hot acidified dichromate gives propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which explains the C=O at 1700 cm-1 and broad carboxyl O-H at 2500-3000 cm-1 in Q.
options.B: Propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$, is a ketone and would also show C=O near 1720 cm-1, but ketones are not oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI). It could not form a carboxylic acid Q, so this is the aldehyde versus ketone trap.
options.C: Propan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is a primary alcohol. It would show hydroxy O-H at 3200-3600 cm-1 and C-O at 1040-1300 cm-1, not a strong C=O at 1720 cm-1. Although it can be oxidised fully to an acid, the IR of P rules it out.
options.D: Propan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, is a secondary alcohol. It would show hydroxy O-H, not C=O in P, and with hot dichromate it gives propanone, a ketone, not a carboxylic acid. So both the P and Q spectra rule it out.
